Construct noun keeps only its own words; the phrase's single the is the rectum's article's, English fronting it before the anarthrous rendering of man (rule 29). Head on first by rule 31's subtraction, though first born is close to a tie and heading on born was available.

The rectum's article takes the the the ASV writes for the chain, even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously, exactly as in luchot ha'avanim (rule 29). Marking it unrepresented is reserved for a phrase for which the ASV writes no the at all.

Construct noun keeps only its own word; the phrase's the is the rectum's article's under rule 29's fronting, the rectum being rendered anarthrously as unclean beasts.

The article on behemah takes the written the, fronted before the anarthrous rendering of the rectum (rule 29); as the first article of the noun phrase it takes it before the agreement article does (rule 47).
Nomen rectum takes of, discontinuous around the attributive (rules 19, 25).

review_notes: Corrected: in 'the first born of man' and 'the firstling of unclean beasts' the ASV writes one the with an anarthrous rectum, which is rule 29's fronting case. The article morpheme on the rectum takes that the (s026 to t023, s031 to t033) and the construct keeps only its own word; the accepted alignment had given the construct a supplied the and marked the article unrepresented, which rule 29 allows only where the ASV writes no the for the phrase at all.
The agreement article on hattemeah remains unrepresented, the noun's own article having taken the phrase's single the (rule 47).
'both of man and beast' gives both ... and to the single waw, since no other morpheme in the clause is what both says (rule 14).
The second bet and both assimilated articles are unrepresented: the ASV writes one of and no the for either noun (rules 22, 29, 40).
